claim.why_it_matters: The figure's table places Margin C over position 6 (it is between 6 and 7), Margin A over position 8 (it is between 7 and 8) and Margin R over '...'; the area labels are listed in the wrong order ('Program-text Area Sequence Number Area') with no mapping to positions. The figure as transcribed misstates the fixed-form layout; only the prose below it is correct.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered PDF page 46 (printed p.24, §2002:6.2 Figure 1) at 300 dpi: Margin L is a bar left of position 1; Margin C is a bar between positions 6 and 7; Margin A a bar between 7 and 8; Margin R a bar right of '...'. A brace under 1-6 is labelled 'Sequence Number Area', an arrow at 7 'Indicator Area', a brace under 8..13 ... 'Program-text Area'. The markdown table puts 'Margin C' in the column of position 6, 'Margin A' in the column of position 8, 'Margin R' in the '...' column, merges 9-13 into one cell, and emits the area labels as 'Program-text Area Sequence Number Area' / 'Indicator Area' with no position mapping and in reversed order. The claim quotes both sources accurately. The transcribed figure misstates the margin positions (Margin C over column 6 reads as column 6 belonging to margin C rather than the boundary 6|7). Mitigation: the prose immediately below the figure (Margin C between 6th and 7th, Margin A between 7th and 8th, sequence number 1-6, indicator 7, program text from 8) is transcribed correctly and carries the same content, so a reader using the prose is not misled; the defect is confined to the figure.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as described. Figure 1 (§2002:6.2) is mistranscribed as a table that places Margin C over position 6, Margin A over position 8 and Margin R over '...' instead of on the boundaries 6|7, 7|8 and after the last position, and lists the area labels in reversed order without mapping them to positions 1-6, 7 and 8+. The prose following the figure is correct and restates every position, so the defect is limited to the figure's depiction (no normative rule is lost).
